candidates.title: Animal Friends: Reptile Rescuer John Hale
candidates.audiences: Kids (6-11); Pre-schoolers (3-5); Toddlers (18 mos. to 3 yrs); Tweens (11-13)
candidates.description: Join PACL and Project HumaneKind as we host reptile rescuer John Hale at the Children's Library! John will introduce several wonderous creatures we share the Earth with. You might meet: Bernie the Chameleon, Ginger the Bearded Dragon, Vince the Red-Footed Tortoise, or Cupcake the Rabbit. Surprises abound! Please arrive on time. Project HumaneKind teaches compassion and respect for living beings. Through humane education, they combat cruelty and indifference and bring awareness to the intelligent, social, and emotional depths of our fellow animals. Visit them online at www.projecthumanekind.org .
candidates.tips:

candidates.title: Festival of Lights: A Diwali Celebration
candidates.audiences: Adults; Babies (under 2); Kids (6-11); Pre-schoolers (3-5); Seniors; Teens (14-18); Toddlers (18 mos. to 3 yrs); Tweens (11-13)
candidates.description:
Join us at the Mitchell Park Community Center, as we celebrate Diwali! Enjoy fun activities for all ages including:

 Ongoing from 2-4 PM:
 Henna with teaching artist Rachel-Anne Palacios (Adobe Room; henna line closes at 3:30 PM !) Rangoli (chalk coloring craft outside in the Courtyard) Crafts (in Adobe Room) All activities available while supplies last!
 Performance from 2:30-3:30 PM in El Palo Alto Room by Noorani Dance .

Rachel-Anne Palacios is an Afro-Chicana Oakland native, multi-cultural arts educator, and self-taught folk artist. She has been teaching art workshops and classes at Bay Area schools and libraries for over a decade and a half and her lessons and projects are inspired by indigenous cultures and traditional art from around the world.

 Noorani Dance , founded in 2016 by by international Kathak artist, Farah Yasmeen Shaikh, exemplifies Farah’s unique artistic expression and vision coupled with the classical and innovative influence and style of Farah's Guru, the late Pandit Chitresh Das. "Noorani" means bright or luminous, with a dual meaning of enlightenment. With Kathak dance as their medium, Noorani Dance is committed to enlightening minds and hearts through the arts.

candidates.title: LOCATION CHANGE: Mindfulness Meditation
candidates.audiences: Adults; Babies (under 2); Kids (6-11); Pre-schoolers (3-5); Seniors; Teens (14-18); Toddlers (18 mos. to 3 yrs); Tweens (11-13)
candidates.description: **Note: The December 5th meditation session will be at the Palo Alto Art Center. This session is open to all ages. Come and improve your mental and physical health in mindfulness meditation sessions led by Phuong Pham. Each session is 30 minutes of sitting meditation and 15 minutes of releasing meditation followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and Q&A. Chairs are available for those who do not bring them. Phuong is a Buddhist nun experienced in leading mindfulness meditation. You can learn more about Phuong here and can watch her meditation videos on the library's YouTube channel here .
candidates.tips:
Kids under 10 need an adult with them.**.
It is open to all levels of experience and no registration required.
Bring yoga mats and/or meditation cushions.

candidates.title: Animal Friends: Meet a Chicken with Isabelle Cnudde
candidates.audiences: Kids (6-11); Pre-schoolers (3-5); Toddlers (18 mos. to 3 yrs); Tweens (11-13)
candidates.description: Did you know chickens can recognize over 100 faces, dream when they sleep, and even see more colors than we do? Join Project HumaneKind at the Palo Alto Children's Library as we meet Clorofil's Isabelle Cnudde and one of her feathered friends. Come discover their natural behaviors, their big personalities, and what makes them such cool animals. Coloring pages will be available for the attendees. Please arrive on time. As founder of Clorofil, and animal advocacy nonprofit and micro-sanctuary, Isabelle rescues chickens and gives them a safe home where they can just be chickens. Learn more about them at www.clorofil.org . Project HumaneKind teaches compassion and respect for living beings. Through humane education, they combat cruelty and indifference and bring awareness to the intelligent, social, and emotional depths of our fellow animals. Visit them online at www.projecthumanekind.org .
